props.text: The Lantern Theatre: A Restoration in Four Frames

For three years, the 1921 Lantern Theatre sat behind scaffolding and plywood while crews worked to bring back its gilded proscenium, hand-painted ceiling, and original oak seating. These four images follow the work from first demolition to the reopening night.

props.alt: Workers removing plaster from the theatre's east wall to expose original lath

props.text: Stripping decades of plaster from the east wall revealed the original lath and hand-mixed lime mortar beneath.

props.alt: Restorer applying gold leaf to a carved column capital in the auditorium

props.text: A restorer applies 23-karat gold leaf to a carved capital, matching a pattern found in the 1921 archives.

props.alt: Ceiling mural partially uncovered with conservators working on scaffolding

props.text: Conservators clean the ceiling mural one square foot at a time, using cotton swabs and solvent gels.

props.alt: Audience filling restored seats on opening night under warm house lights

props.text: On reopening night, the restored house lights came up over 480 seats refinished in their original oak.

props.alt: The reopened Lantern Theatre auditorium at dusk, with its restored proscenium lit for a performance

props.text: Restoration was completed on March 14, 2024, when the Lantern Theatre's gilded proscenium and hand-painted ceiling were lit for the first full season.
